newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says studying NATO command proposal.
newsitem.headline: France says studying NATO command proposal.

text.p: France said on Wednesday it was studying a German proposal to resolve a row with the United States on NATO's southern command, adding that it was keen to end the dispute.
The United States opened the door on Tuesday to the possibility of giving up or sharing the command of southern NATO forces with Europe after a delay of perhaps five years.
Germany had earlier announced a tentative plan to resolve the row over French demands that Washington hand over or share the Naples-based command with Europe.
"Exchanges are naturally taking place with our American allies as with our European allies," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.
"There are different formulas on the table and we are examining them with a will to reach an agreement," he added.

German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe suggested on Tuesday that a face-saving deal for France was emerging in Europe to leave the command in U.S. hands now but reconsider the issue in five or six years, while strengthening European participation in the region.

The divisive debate over France's demand to put a European in charge of the strategically important post had jeopardised an earlier pledge by Paris that its military forces would rejoin NATO's military structure after an absence of over 30 years.
"If there is no solution before the Madrid (NATO summit in July), France will leave its relations with NATO unchanged," Rummelhardt said.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said on a visit to Bonn on Tuesday that Washington was willing to review the matter in five, six or seven years, but suggested the command might still remain in U.S. hands.
